countries_thin_or_null: Brunei — DSBB and related primary pages continue to describe national accounts as compiled in accordance with the 1993/2008 System of National Accounts hybrid; training in full 2008 SNA and sequence of accounts still listed as medium-term needs; no primary confirmation of completed pure 2008 SNA transition

Timor-Leste — strongest primary methodology statements remain the 2012 National Accounts volumes (explicitly 2008 SNA + BPM6 + COICOP); post-2023 INETL restructuring and 2025 ASEAN accession have not yet produced newer public methodology pages superseding those

proposed_reports.title: Cambodia National Accounts Base-Year Update (2014)
proposed_reports.description: 2014 base-year rebase of Cambodian national accounts, announced and disseminated by NIS in 2024; replaces prior 1993 SNA / ISIC Rev. 3 framework with 2008 SNA and ISIC Rev. 4; roadmap for next rebase to 2024 base year planned for 2026.

proposed_reports.title: Timor-Leste National Accounts 2004-2010 Methodological Notes (Volume II)
proposed_reports.description: Companion methodological volume to Timor-Leste’s National Accounts 2004-2010; documents concepts, sources and methods used in compilation under 2008 SNA and BPM6 frameworks, including COICOP classification for household consumption.
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: one-time methodological companion (reference for subsequent series)

dependencies.basis: NIS Director-General stated that the 2014 base-year update of national accounts is based on the 2008 National Accounting Statistics System (SNA 2008) and ISIC Revision 4, replacing the prior 1993 SNA / ISIC 3 framework.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The 2014 base year is based on the ‘2008 National Accounting Statistics System’ and the ‘International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities [ISIC 4]’, which replaced the outdated ISIC 3 and the 1993 National Accounting System.

dependencies.basis: Timor-Leste National Accounts (2004-2010 series and subsequent) are compiled in accordance with the System of National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA); methodological notes explicitly adopt 2008 SNA concepts, definitions and classifications.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The estimates of Timor-Leste’s National Accounts (TL-NA) 2004-2010 are based on the concepts and classifications of the System of National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA), and the sixth edition of the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6).

dependencies.basis: National accounts compilation is harmonized with BPM6 for services, primary incomes, current transfers and related external-sector linkages.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The estimates of Timor-Leste’s National Accounts (TL-NA) 2004-2010 are based on the concepts and classifications of the System of National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA), and the sixth edition of the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6).

dependencies.basis: Household final consumption expenditures are classified according to COICOP (level 3 classes, with further breakdown where available).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Household final consumption expenditures are classified according to the COICOP at level 3– classes, and, where available and appropriate also at the imputed level 4 (six digits).

dependencies.basis: Supply and Use Tables and Input-Output Tables are compiled as an integral part of the System of National Accounts 2008; the broader national accounts series incorporate 1993/2008 SNA recommendations to the extent relevant, with ongoing training toward fuller 2008 SNA implementation.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Supply and Use Tables are an integral part of the System of National Accounts 2008, jointly produced by the United Nations, International Monetary Fund, World Bank, Organisation for the Economic Cooperation and Development and the European Union.
